result:
Both plates are modelled and exported, and no step failed.

- **Plate 80:** I drew an 80 × 50 mm rectangle on XY with one corner at the origin and extruded it 5 mm. I then cut four Ø5 holes at (8,8), (72,8), (8,42) and (72,42), plus a Ø12 hole at (40,25). The bounding box is 80 × 50 × 5. The volume is 19,041.9 mm³, which matches the hand calculation. It's exported to `/lab/out/plate-80.stl`.
- **Plate 60:** I rebuilt the plate at 60 mm wide, with the corner holes at x = 8 and 52 and the Ø12 hole at (30,25). The bounding box is 60 × 50 × 5 and the volume is 14,041.9 mm³. It's exported to `/lab/out/plate-60.stl`.

**How I made the 60 mm plate:** it's a fresh design (`new_design`), not an edit of the 80 mm one. Sketch coordinates don't accept parameter expressions (`"width - 8"` was rejected), and I didn't add dimensions to the sketches. So the hole positions don't follow a width parameter. A `width` parameter I created in the first design was lost when I started the new one.

The first design is no longer open, and I didn't save either design as a `.solidcraft` file. Only the two STL files exist.
